rationale: X matches the references and fully serves the maintainer: it accurately explains the trailing-only decision, the strict plain-`Hash` default, subclass opt-in, mutation via `pop`, fresh `{}` miss result, and why earlier hashes remain positional. It also verifies the explanation with the focused Active Support test file and a direct behavioral probe, reaching parity or better on investigation. The only factual overstatement is that opt-in is necessarily per class rather than per instance; Ruby singleton-method dispatch permits an individual hash-subclass instance to override the predicate, but that edge does not undermine the requested subclass contract.

shortcomings.summary: It overstates opt-in as exclusively per-class.
shortcomings.evidence: `.amp/judge-inputs/L04/X.md:42` says opt-in is per class, not per instance. The implementation calls `last.extractable_options?` dynamically at `activesupport/lib/active_support/core_ext/array/extract_options.rb:27-31`; judge probe `def h.extractable_options? = true` on one `Hash`-subclass instance produced `[true, true]` for same-object extraction and an emptied receiver, so singleton per-instance opt-in is possible.

strengths.summary: It explains the exact two-gate, trailing-only contract without ambiguity.
strengths.evidence: `.amp/judge-inputs/L04/X.md:3-32` reproduces the implementation and shows both an earlier-hash miss and a two-hash last-only extraction. This matches `activesupport/lib/active_support/core_ext/array/extract_options.rb:4-33`.

strengths.summary: It correctly distinguishes plain Hash behavior from conservative subclass behavior and the supported opt-in mechanism.
strengths.evidence: `.amp/judge-inputs/L04/X.md:34-42` explains `instance_of?(Hash)` versus `is_a?(Hash)` and names framework opt-ins. Definitions exist in `activesupport/lib/active_support/hash_with_indifferent_access.rb:70-73`, `ordered_options.rb:64`, and `ordered_hash.rb:42`; test fixtures at `activesupport/test/core_ext/array/extract_options_test.rb:9-16,25-55` cover rejection and opt-in extraction.

strengths.summary: It clearly covers mutation, object identity, miss behavior, and positional intent with executed evidence.
strengths.evidence: `.amp/judge-inputs/L04/X.md:44-62` states that success returns and removes the same object while failure returns a fresh mutable plain Hash without changing the receiver. `.amp/judge-inputs/L04/X.thread.md:130-176` runs the focused suite (`5 runs, 11 assertions, 0 failures`) and a probe for earlier hashes, two hashes, subclass misses, fresh miss hashes, and same-object hits.
